scan.summary: This is your own 2025 annual report under your Standard Air Contaminant Discharge Permit, plus DEQ's automatic email saying it was received on February 12, 2026. It is your proof that you filed on time. DEQ says plainly that the email confirms receipt only and is not a finding that the report is complete or that you met the permit. The report covers 2025 throughput, the scrubber pressure-drop summary, the quarterly inspections, the C-1 carbon changeout and weekly checks, and one deviation that was reported (the S-2 pump failure in August 2025). The one thing to follow up on now: the report set the next C-1 carbon replacement for on or before March 14, 2026, and that date has passed.
scan.freshness_note: This is the report for 2025, filed February 2026. It is the latest one you would expect to have until the 2026 report is due, probably in early 2027 (see deadlines). Nothing newer is needed for this report. You should, however, find the record showing the C-1 carbon was replaced on or before March 14, 2026, because this report sets that date and nothing in your file list shows it happened.

The identity details come from page 1 (sender, date, permit number, submission ID) and pages 2 and 3 (report heading, sections, and the February 10, 2026 signature). I am confident about what the report says. Two limits: I have not seen the permit itself, so I cannot check that the report covers everything Condition 4.1 asks for, or when the 2026 report is due. The five-year retention end date and the waste point about spent carbon are my own reasoning, not text in the document. As a record, this report looks complete for 2025. The only open item is the March 14, 2026 carbon replacement, which this document cannot confirm. Your existing C-1 detector-tube log for August–September 2026 suggests the unit is still running. Nothing here says whether DEQ accepted the report; the email confirms receipt only.

Quarterly inspections under Condition 3.2 were carried out on March 27, June 26, September 25 and
December 18, 2025, and are recorded in the scrubber maintenance file.
3. Carbon adsorption unit C-1 (Condition 3.3)
The carbon in C-1 was replaced on March 14, 2025 (Calgon Filtrasorb 400, 1,800 pounds, by Northwest
Carbon Services). Weekly detector-tube checks at the C-1 outlet were carried out every week in 2025 with
no breakthrough detected. The next scheduled replacement is on or before March 14, 2026.
4. Deviations and excess emissions (Conditions 5.1 and 5.2)
One deviation. On August 22, 2025 the S-2 recirculation pump failed at 14:10; the caustic repackaging
line was stopped within four minutes and remained down until the pump was replaced on August 24. No
product was repackaged on the caustic line while the scrubber was out of service. The Department was
notified by email on August 23, 2025 and a written report was submitted on September 2, 2025 (DEQ
reference DEV-2025-0913).
Opacity: no visible emissions above 20 percent were observed at any permitted source in 2025.
I certify that the information in this report is true, accurate and complete to the best of my knowledge.
Daniel Okafor, Plant Manager · Signed: February 10, 2026
